content: Community Health Workers (CHWs) are individuals who are deeply integrated into the communities they serve and are trusted by those communities. They act as a vital link between healthcare systems and populations that are often underserved or marginalized. Their responsibilities include conducting outreach efforts to engage community members, advocating for the needs and rights of individuals within the community, and providing social support to those in need. Additionally, they play a key role in delivering health education to improve awareness and understanding of health-related issues. CHWs also assist in connecting individuals to appropriate healthcare services through referrals. In certain situations, they may carry out specific clinical tasks, but only under the direct supervision of licensed healthcare professionals.
